name: file.read
description: Read the contents of a file. Supports whole-file or chunked partial reads (via offset + length). Text encodings are decoded server-side; `binary` returns raw bytes base64-encoded.

path.description: Absolute path. Windows accepts forward or back slashes; long paths via \\?\ on NT 5.1+.

encoding.description: Encoding used to decode the bytes. `binary` returns raw bytes base64-encoded; all others decode server-side and `content` is the decoded text.

offset.description: Byte offset to start reading from.

length.description: Maximum number of bytes to read. If omitted, reads to end of file.

content.description: Decoded text in the requested encoding, or base64-encoded raw bytes when `encoding: binary`.

bytes_read.description: Byte length of the content returned (after decoding for text encodings, or the original-bytes length for binary). Distinct from `file.stat.size` (the total file size).

truncated.description: True when `length` was supplied AND the file had more bytes after `offset + length`. False when the read reached EOF (including the case where `length` is omitted).

x-implementations.name: create_file_w
x-implementations.description: Win32 `CreateFileW` (Unicode path) + `SetFilePointerEx` (offset) + `ReadFile` (length-bounded). Long-path opt-in via the `\\?\` prefix on NT 5.1+.

x-implementations.name: create_file_a
x-implementations.description: Win32 `CreateFileA` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x where CreateFileW is unavailable. ANSI path; transcoded UTF-8 → ANSI by the agent.

windows-modern.description: CreateFileW + ReadFile. Decodes server-side per `encoding`; long paths via `\\?\` prefix automatic when input exceeds MAX_PATH. UTF-16LE is native Windows wide-char; cp1252 covers legacy Windows ANSI files.

windows-classic.description: CreateFileA on NT 4 / 9x; CreateFileW on NT 5+. No long-path support pre-NT-5.1 — paths over MAX_PATH return ERR not_found. UTF-16LE/BE decoding implemented in-agent (NT-era Win32 has no MultiByteToWideChar for arbitrary encodings); cp1252 on classic uses GetCPInfoEx + locale-aware conversion.
